headline: Regional Beach Access and Vehicle Permit System Overview
reservation: Access to specific beaches and state parks often requires a regional permit or daily parking pass, distinct from overnight accommodation bookings. During peak summer months, popular locations like Robert Moses or Montauk may reach capacity; check official New York State Parks and local township portals for the latest entry requirements.

days.title: Maritime Sentinels and South Shore Dunes

stops.name: Fire Island Lighthouse
stops.detail: Walk from Field 5 at Robert Moses State Park to explore this historic beacon and its surrounding boardwalks through rare coastal dunes.

stops.name: Southampton Village
stops.detail: Visit for a stroll through historic colonial architecture and local maritime heritage sites.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours; conditions vary significantly with seasonal traffic
days.note: The 'Trade Parade' traffic can impact travel times; plan movements between 10 AM and 2 PM when possible.

days.title: Rugged Bluffs of The End

stops.name: Montauk Point Lighthouse
stops.detail: Explore the oldest lighthouse in New York State, commissioned by George Washington, situated at the island's easternmost tip.

stops.name: Camp Hero State Park
stops.detail: Hike the dramatic bluffs where the glacial moraine meets the Atlantic Ocean for rugged coastal views.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours; conditions vary on Montauk Highway
days.note: Coastal winds are frequent; carry layers even in mid-summer.

days.title: North Fork Pastoral Heritage
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Montauk via Shelter Island Ferry

stops.name: Greenport Village
stops.detail: Wander the historic seaport, visit the maritime museum, and see the 1920s antique carousel.

stops.name: North Fork Wineries
stops.detail: Drive Route 25 to see the region's agricultural roots and family-owned vineyards.

days.driving: Allow 2.5 hours including ferry transfers; conditions vary
days.note: Ferry wait times vary; check the North Ferry schedule for current crossing frequency.

intel.title: Beach Permits
intel.text: Many beaches require township-specific stickers; non-resident daily passes are available at Robert Moses and Montauk Point State Parks. Check for mobile payment app availability at local town lots.

intel.title: Coastal Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular reception is generally stable, though remote sections of the Hither Hills and Sunken Forest may experience gaps. Download maps for the eastern bluffs.

intel.title: East End Supply
intel.text: Station density decreases significantly east of Amagansett on the South Fork. Ensure adequate supply before entering the more remote park areas of Montauk.

intel.title: Peak Season Crowds
intel.text: Weekends in July and August see the highest visitation. Early morning arrivals are suggested for popular state park beach parking.

intel.title: Island Transfers
intel.text: The Shelter Island Ferry connects the North and South Forks, bypassing mainland traffic. This is a vehicle ferry service requiring on-board payment.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at ISP and drive 20 minutes to the south shore; stock up on coastal essentials in Babylon or Bay Shore.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for all paved routes; check rental contracts for restrictions on unpaved beach access roads.
plan.goldenHour: Navy Beach on Fort Pond Bay for sunset, noting that visibility is season-dependent.
